info.name: CMS · All roles
info.description:
End-to-end test of the clinic API for all seven roles. A new patient books an appointment; the
receptionist, doctor, nurse and pharmacist each do their part of the visit and its billing; the admin
and lab technician do theirs. A permission matrix then checks every role against every permission,
and the ownership folder checks that patients and doctors reach only their own data.

Before running:
1. deployment/keycloak_setup.sh (roles, group, clients, the API's audience, token rules)
2. deployment/seed.sh (clinic data and one login per role)
3. Start the API on port 1300, in development (not the prod profile)

The logins here go through the API's password endpoints (POST /auth/login and the rest), which exist for
API clients such as this collection: on in development (PASSWORD_ENDPOINTS on the API and PASSWORD_LOGIN
in keycloak_setup.sh, both true by default) and off in production, where current OAuth guidance
(RFC 9700) rules the password grant out and the web app signs everyone in on Keycloak's page. Each login
checks that the token names the API as its audience; the sessions folder checks that a refresh token
works once. Staff invited through POST /staff have two-factor sign-in to set up first and cannot log in
here until they have; the seeded logins are not affected.

Run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner; later requests use ids saved by earlier
ones. Each run registers a new patient, books the next free slot, registers one walk-in and adds one
medicine (discontinued again at the end). No emails are sent: forgot-password is only tried with an
unknown address.

item.name: 12 · Permission matrix
item.description: Every role against one request per permission. Requests use invalid bodies or ids that don't exist, so an allowed call stops at validation or lookup (400/404) and nothing changes; a denied one gets 403.
